headerDisplay: The **Homebridge SmartHQ** plugin allows you to interact with SmartHQ devices from HomeKit and Siri.
footerDisplay:
Your SmartHQ account was linked. Please raise any issues on our [project page](https://github.com/homebridge-plugins/homebridge-smarthq/issues).

If you would like to have other features, please open a [feature request](https://github.com/homebridge-plugins/homebridge-smarthq/issues/new/choose).

mfaCode.title: 2FA Verification Code
mfaCode.description: Only needed if your SmartHQ account has two-factor authentication (2FA) turned on. When login fails asking for a code, check your email or phone for the code, enter it here, then restart Homebridge. After one successful login the plugin saves a token and this box can be left empty.

notice.title: Notice
notice.default: Keep your username and password a secret!

configDeviceName.title: Device Name
configDeviceName.description: This is the name that will be used to identify the device in HomeKit.

serialNumber.title: Serial Number
serialNumber.description: Optional. The serial number shown on the appliance's own label. SmartHQ does not hold a serial number for every appliance, and HomeKit shows 'Unknown' when it does not. The plugin asks the appliance itself first, so only fill this in if HomeKit still shows 'Unknown'.

hide_device.title: Hide Device
hide_device.description: If enabled, the device will not be added to HomeKit.

useMatter.title: Enable Matter
useMatter.description: Not currently available. Homebridge has no Matter device type for ovens, dishwashers, washers or dryers, so every SmartHQ appliance falls back to HomeKit (HAP) regardless of this setting. Kept so existing configuration files stay valid, and hidden from this form until Homebridge gains those device types.

matterOnly.title: Matter Only (No HAP Fallback)
matterOnly.description: Not currently available, and unsafe to enable: because no SmartHQ appliance has a Matter device type in Homebridge, turning this on stops the accessory being published at all. Kept so existing configuration files stay valid, and hidden from this form.

keurig.title: Keurig K-Cup Hot Water Services
keurig.description: Enable HomeKit services for the built-in Keurig K-Cup brewer on refrigerators that have one (e.g. PYE22PYNHFS). Leave unset to auto-detect from the appliance. Set false to disable even on supported models. Set true to force-enable if auto-detect misfires.

keurigOnly.title: Keurig Only (Hide Main Refrigerator)
keurigOnly.description: On a refrigerator with a built-in Keurig, skip the main Refrigerator HomeKit accessory and publish only the Keurig sub-accessory. Useful if you only care about the coffee maker and want to declutter Apple Home.

refreshRate.title: Device Refresh Rate
refreshRate.description: Indicates the number of seconds between polls of the SmartHQ service.

logging.title: Device Logging Level Override
logging.description: Overrides the plugin logging level for this device only. None turns off all messages from this plugin. Standard shows normal activity, warnings and errors. Debug adds detailed messages, and is what to use when reporting a problem. Default behaves the same as Standard.

defaultOperationMode.title: Default Operation Mode (Air Conditioners)
defaultOperationMode.description: The SmartHQ mode applied when the air conditioner service is switched on in HomeKit. Only applies to air conditioners.

createSeparateFanService.title: Separate Fan Service (Air Conditioners)
createSeparateFanService.description: If enabled, a separate fan service is exposed for fan-speed control (0% = auto, 1-33% = low, 34-66% = medium, 67-100% = high). Only applies to air conditioners.

showDryModeSwitch.title: Show Dry Mode Switch (Air Conditioners)
showDryModeSwitch.description: If disabled, the dry mode switch is not exposed in HomeKit. Only applies to air conditioners.

showHeatMode.title: Show Heat Mode (Air Conditioners)
showHeatMode.description: If disabled, heat is removed from the HomeKit mode selector and the heat mode switch is not exposed. Turn this off for cooling-only models. Only applies to air conditioners.

showModeSwitches.title: Show Mode Switches (Air Conditioners)
showModeSwitches.description: If disabled, the individual mode switches (cool, heat, fan only, dry, energy saver) are hidden for a minimal tile. Note: heat and cool stay available in the HomeKit mode selector, but Apple's selector cannot hold the other modes — those would then only be reachable from the SmartHQ app. Only applies to air conditioners.

showBakeSwitch.title: Show Bake Switch
showBakeSwitch.description: Ovens only: expose a switch that starts a Bake at the target temperature. The oven thermostat already does this through its Heat mode, so this is only needed if you want a dedicated tile.

showConvBakeMultiSwitch.title: Show Convection Bake Multi Switch
showConvBakeMultiSwitch.description: Ovens only: expose a switch that starts Convection Bake Multi at the target temperature.

showConvRoastSwitch.title: Show Convection Roast Switch
showConvRoastSwitch.description: Ovens only: expose a switch that starts Convection Roast at the target temperature.

showAirFrySwitch.title: Show Air Fry Switch
showAirFrySwitch.description: Ovens only: expose a switch that starts Air Fry at the target temperature. Only ovens with an Air Fry mode will respond.

cookModeCavity.title: Mode Switches Control
cookModeCavity.description: Double ovens only: which cavity the mode switches above start. Many double ovens only offer Convection Bake, Convection Roast and Air Fry in the lower oven - if the switches do nothing on yours, pick Lower Oven.

showRunningSwitch.title: Show Running Switch
showRunningSwitch.description: Washers, dryers, and combination washer/dryers only: expose a read-only switch that shows whether the machine is running.

showEnergy.title: Show Estimated Energy Use
showEnergy.description: Any appliance: add a tile showing ESTIMATED power (W) and total energy (kWh). SmartHQ reports no real power readings, so the plugin works them out from what the appliance does report - cycle phase, mode, setting and temperatures. On washers and dryers this tile replaces the Show Running Switch tile, so re-select it in any automations. Coffee makers, microwaves, Advantium ovens, beverage centres and water softeners show a fixed average until the plugin reads their state.

energyProtocol.title: Energy Tile Protocol
energyProtocol.description: Matter only (recommended on iOS/iPadOS 27 or later): the tile is a Matter outlet (always On for always-on appliances like fridges and filters) with power and energy measurement. Apple Home shows the watts on the tile and in its Energy view. Needs Homebridge 2.2.1 or later with Matter enabled for this bridge, and the bridge's Matter QR code added to Apple Home. The appliance's other tiles stay as they are. If Matter is unavailable the plugin falls back to HAP and logs why. HAP: an outlet with Eve power characteristics. Apple Home shows only On/Off; the Eve, Controller for HomeKit and Home+ apps show the watts and kWh.

oneOf.title: Matter only (Apple Home shows watts, iOS 27+)

showEnergyInHome.title: Show Watts In Apple Home
showEnergyInHome.description: HAP only. Apple Home cannot display HAP power readings, so this adds a light sensor linked to the running tile whose lux reading is the estimated watts (e.g. 1230 lx = 1230 W). Turn on "Show as Single Tile" for the accessory in the Home app to keep it with the running tile. Not needed with Matter.

energyStandbyWatts.title: Standby / Average Power (W)
energyStandbyWatts.description: Idle draw. For always-on appliances (fridge, beverage centre, filter, softener) the average over a day. Leave blank for the appliance default - see the README for each appliance's defaults.

energyMotorWatts.title: Motor / Fan / Pump Power (W)
energyMotorWatts.description: Drum motor (laundry), wash pump (dishwasher), fan (hood, AC, ice maker), turbo boost (fridge), or the lower cavity element (double oven). Leave blank for the default.

energySpinWatts.title: Spin Power (W)
energySpinWatts.description: Washers and washer/dryers only: draw during high-speed spin. Default 400.

energyHeaterWatts.title: Heater / Main Load Power (W)
energyHeaterWatts.description: The main load at full output: water heater (washer 1800, dishwasher 1200), dryer element (2400; heat pump dryer about 700, gas 0), oven element (3500), induction burner (2200), AC or ice maker compressor (900 / 120), water heater (550 heat pump; 4500 for an element tank), Keurig tank (700). Use 0 for a hot-fed top-loading washer.

showFilterBattery.title: Show Filter Life As Battery
showFilterBattery.description: Water filters only: expose the filter life percentage as a battery. The Home app shows this on the accessory's settings screen rather than as a tile of its own, and warns you when it drops to 10%.

refreshRate.title: Refresh Rate
refreshRate.description: Indicates the number of seconds between polls of the Meater service.

logging.title: Plugin Logging Level
logging.description: None turns off all messages from this plugin. Standard shows normal activity, warnings and errors. Debug adds detailed messages, and is what to use when reporting a problem. Default behaves the same as Standard.

region.title: Account Region
region.description: The region of your SmartHQ account. Leave as default unless the login page resolves to the wrong region (for example a US account behind European DNS).

allowInvalidCharacters.title: Allow Invalid Characters
allowInvalidCharacters.description: Keep accessory names exactly as the provider reports them. Without this, characters HomeKit does not accept are stripped out and the change is reported in the log.

energyCostPerKwh.title: Electricity Rate (per kWh)
energyCostPerKwh.description: What you pay per kWh, used for the estimated cost on the Energy dashboard. Leave blank to hide costs.

energyCurrency.title: Currency Symbol
energyCurrency.description: Shown before costs on the Energy dashboard, e.g. $, £ or €.

items.helpvalue: This is for Manual Setup Only.

Refresh Rate
Refresh Rate indicates the number of seconds between polls of the SmartHQ service.

Homekit Controller Notifications Secret
For better notifications you can configure homekit controller, this is the secret under 'Devices & Secret'

Account Region
Set this if the SmartHQ login resolves to the wrong region for your account.

Energy Dashboard
Your electricity rate and currency, for the estimated costs on the Energy tab.
